newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end firm, nudging 6.75 pct yield.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end firm, nudging 6.75 pct yield.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended strongly higher Tuesday, barely looking back following a morning runup on softer than expected manufacturing data.
But bond prices met stiff resistance near the 6.75 percent cash yield, futures traders said. The 30-year cash bond was yielding 6.74 percent in the late afternoon.
After the initial spike higher, bond futures remained buoyant throughout the session on a combination of short-covering and speculative buying, traders said.
"There has been a consistent bid here all day long," a Treasury bond futures broker said late in the session.
September Treasury bond futures posted a new high of 111-29/32 late in the day before closing just off the highs.
Prices initially spiked upward on news the National Association of Purchasing Management reported its business index slipped to 55.7 in June from 57.1 in May.
"That was the main engine behind the rally," said a brokerage trader.
Traders and analysts had expected a stronger June NAPM number, especially given the unexpected strength seen in the Chicago purchasers report Monday.
"They had bad expectations due to yesterday's report," the brokerage trader said.
But key components in the national data were softer and helped calm jitters about the economy accelerating, he said. Production, new orders and price measures all eased from the previous month.
Before this morning's NAPM survey was released, futures were underpinned somewhat by news a 1.8 percent drop in construction spending in May after a 0.3 percent rise in April.
"Construction spending was friendly, but it did not move the market," the trader said.

Traders said sentiment that the Federal Open Market Committee will leave interest rates unchanged at the conclusion of its two-day meeting Wednesday attracted speculative buying interest that helped underpin debt futures.
They noted the fed funds futures price curve foreshadowed steady rates in July and August, but one or possibly two 25-basis-point increases by year-end.

September T-bonds ended 20/32 higher at 111-22/32, July fed funds ended steady at 94.45, August fed funds ended 0.01 point higher also at 94.45, and December Eurodollars ended 0.050 points higher at 93.95.
